requirement.text: Adding a product that is already in the cart increases that line's quantity by one instead of adding a second line.

findings.explanation: addItem in src/cart/cart.js finds an existing line by productId and increments its quantity instead of pushing a new line.

requirement.text: Discount codes are case-insensitive: "SAVE10", "save10" and "Save10" all apply the same 10% discount.

findings.explanation: findDiscount in src/cart/discounts.js only trims whitespace and does a case-sensitive Map lookup against the single key "SAVE10", so inputs like "save10" or "Save10" will not match and return null instead of applying the 10% discount.

requirement.text: When the last item is removed, the cart shows the message "Your cart is empty".

findings.explanation: index.html defines a #cart-empty element with the text "Your cart is empty" and app.js toggles its hidden attribute based on isEmpty(cart), showing it when the cart becomes empty after removal.

requirement.text: Shipping costs $5.00 per order. Orders whose subtotal before discounts is $50.00 or more ship free. An empty cart shows $0.00 shipping.

findings.explanation: In src/checkout/shipping.js, shipping is only free when subtotal is strictly greater than $50 (subtotal > FREE_SHIPPING_FROM), so an order with subtotal exactly $50.00 is charged $5.00 shipping instead of being free as required.

requirement.text: Signed-in customers can open an "Order history" page that lists their past orders with the date and total of each.

findings.explanation: There is no account/order history page, sign-in flow, or any code storing or listing past orders in the shown files (index.html, src/app.js, checkout files) — orders are not even persisted, just confirmed with a message.

requirement.text: The 'Place order' button is disabled unless the cart has at least one item.

quote.snippet: The "Place order" button stays disabled until the cart has at least one item and the email field contains a valid email address (name@domain.tld).

findings.explanation: canPlaceOrder in src/checkout/place-order.js requires the cart to be non-empty, and app.js wires this into the disabled state of the place-order button.

requirement.text: The 'Place order' button is disabled unless the email field contains a valid email address (name@domain.tld).

quote.snippet: The "Place order" button stays disabled until the cart has at least one item and the email field contains a valid email address (name@domain.tld).

findings.explanation: canPlaceOrder in src/checkout/place-order.js only checks that the email field is non-empty (email.trim() !== ""), it does not validate the email format against name@domain.tld, so an invalid string like 'abc' would enable the button.

requirement.text: Clicking the enabled 'Place order' button shows the message 'Thanks! Your order is placed.'

quote.snippet: Once it is enabled, clicking it shows "Thanks! Your order is placed."

findings.explanation: The checkout-form submit handler in src/app.js sets the order-confirmation text to 'Thanks! Your order is placed.' when the form (with the enabled place-order button) is submitted.
